newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgaria offers up to 325 bln lvs T-bills Apr14-18.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria offers up to 325 bln lvs T-bills Apr14-18.

text.p: Bulgaria's Finance Ministry will offer 10 issues of one-week and four-week discount T-bills with a total par of up to 325 billion levs and no minimum acceptable price set at auctions this week, the central bank said.

Five issues would have one-week maturity and would be offered with a maximum par value of 25 billion levs each while the five four-week issues will have maximum pars of 40 billion levs, the central bank said in a statement.

"By setting par limits the ministry aims to slow the growth rate of domestic debt while the higher par for the four-week issues is aimed at encouraging investments in longer-term treasuries," a Finance Ministry official told Reuters.
Since January 20 the ministry has been issuing daily one-week and four-week discount T-bills with no par value or a minimum acceptable price set in advance to regulate banks' liquidity.

The issues have been heavily subscribed in the past month because investors opted for high yield lev-denominated instruments as the lev persistently firmed against the dollar on the local interbank market.

Average yields to maturity for four-week T-bills auctioned in the past month ranged between 17.70 and 14.96 percent while yields to maturity for one week paper ranged between 3.84-2.44 percent, central bank figures showed.
The lev traded near 1,500 to the dollar today, up from around 1,600 a month ago.
Details of this week's issues follow. Auction dates and issue dates for each issue overlap.
